raw.body:
@sophiebits Thank you — we tested and **#36779 appears to fix it.**

**Setup**
- Before: Next.js `16.2.6` (bundled `react-dom` without #36779)
- After: Next.js `16.3.0-preview.5`, bundling `react-dom` `19.3.0-canary-247fbb45-20260622` — includes #36779 (merged 2026-06-18)
- Same production-like page (PDP, ~13 streamed boundaries, nested), same staging environment, same `insertBefore` guard probe from my earlier comment. Test harness: a CDP-driven reload loop in a fresh tab (navigate → wait 8s for stream + reveal → `Runtime.evaluate`), classifying each load as ok / guard-trip / renderer-hang (evaluate timeout while the main thread is pinned).

**Results**

| | `16.2.6` (no fix) | `16.3.0-preview.5` (with #36779) |
|---|---|---|
| Outcome | **Renderer hang on the 1st reload** | **100 / 100 reloads clean** |
| `$RV` `insertBefore` calls | (main thread pinned before the 200k guard could dump) | 35–73 per load, never runaway |
| guard trips / hangs | — | 0 / 0 |

On the unfixed build the hang reproduced immediately (1st reload). On the fixed build, 100 consecutive reloads across ~13 min (spanning multiple server-cache warm/cold cycles, so a range of streaming timings) all completed normally, with `$RV` doing the expected small amount of DOM work each time.

**Caveat:** this hang was historically intermittent (repro rate swung 0–90% across hours), so 100 clean reloads is strong but not absolute proof. That said, the contrast — immediate hang before, 100/100 clean after — matches your hypothesis that the stale `nextSegmentId` was the root cause. The client `$RV` runtime is byte-identical between the two builds, consistent with the fix being entirely server-side (the degenerate nested `S`/`B` segment state is no longer produced).

Happy to share the probe script or run additional builds if useful.
